message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules**

| Section | What you need to know |
|---------|-----------------------|
| **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to empty your hand in each round. |
| **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck works best with 4–8). |
| **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. |
| **Setup** | 1. Shuffle the deck. 2. Deal 7 cards to each player. 3. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile. 4. Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two”, the first player draws two cards and loses a turn). |

---

### 1. Turn Order

- Play proceeds clockwise (unless a “Reverse” card changes direction).
- On your turn you may **play one card** that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top discard card, or you may play a Wild card.

### 2. Card Types & Effects

| Card | How to play | Effect |
|------|-------------|--------|
| **Number (0‑9)** | Same color or same number | No special effect |
| **Draw Two** | Same color | Next player draws 2 cards and skips turn |
| **Skip** | Same color | Next player loses their turn |
| **Reverse** | Same color | Reverses play direction (in 2‑player games, acts like a Skip) |
| **Wild** | Any time | Player chooses new color |
| **Wild Draw Four** | Any time (only if you have no matching color) | Player chooses new color; next player draws 4 cards and loses turn |

> **Rule of Thumb:** You may only play a Wild Draw Four if you have no other playable card. If challenged and you *do* have a playable card, the challenger draws 4 cards instead.

### 3. Drawing

- If you cannot play a card, you must draw **one** card from the draw pile.
- If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends.

### 4. “UNO” Call

- When you have **exactly one card left**, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn.
- If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw **two** penalty cards.

### 5. Winning a Round

- The first player to discard all their cards wins the round.
- Score points: sum the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands (number cards = face value, Draw Two/Skip/Reverse = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50).

### 6. Winning the Game

- Play continues until a player reaches the target score (commonly 500).  
- If you’re playing a shorter game, you can set a lower target or play a single round.

---

### Quick Tips

- **Keep an eye on colors** – holding a mix of colors can give you flexibility.
- **Save your Wild Draw Four** for when you’re sure you have no other options; it can be a game‑changer.
- **Watch the discard pile** – if someone plays a “Draw Two” or “Reverse,” you might want to hold onto a matching card to counter‑play.

Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
